build: Epyx original, PAL, two disk sides (C64 Preservation Project, verified dump)

exclude: the processor port's two registers, not memory
runtime: the text screen and its sprite pointers, written by the loader's side prompt and by the menu

the KERNAL's default vectors ($EA31, $FE66 and on): its RESTOR routine at power-on stores each one through the pointer to its own ROM table, which writes the RAM beneath it; the machine's, not the game's
9 parts: The menu, the players and the medals, Hot Dog Aerials, Figure Skating and Free Skating and others
elsewhere: 9 parts: The menu, the players and the medals, Hot Dog Aerials, Figure Skating and Free Skating and others

comments.text: The unpacker's destination pointer, low byte (ldr_unpack, which nothing runs).
The unpacker's destination pointer, high byte.
The unpacker's source pointer, low byte.
The unpacker's source pointer, high byte.
The file number ldr_file_offset was given, kept while it multiplies it by twelve.
The offset of the current file's record in ldr_files (the file number times 12), which ldr_load_file and ldr_run_file index the table with.
The side in the drive as ldr_check_side last read it: 1, 2, 4 or 0. ldr_load_file ANDs it with the side the file's record wants.
Where ldr_get_block stores its next 240-byte block, low byte then high at $0018 (ldr_get_block runs for nothing in this game).
The high byte of ldr_get_block's store pointer.
The third byte of a drive command, from X (a track, or the file's letter for command 2).
The fourth byte of a drive command, from Y (a sector).
The second byte of every drive command, and the number of blocks ldr_get_block counts down. Nothing in the loader writes it, so the drive code is sent whatever the KERNAL left there.
The processor port's value, kept while ldr_get_block banks the I/O out to store a block.
The byte ldr_send_byte is sending, shifted right one bit for each of the two lines.
Where ldr_load_by_name stores the file's next byte: the load address the drive code sends first, low byte, then high at $0023.
The high byte of ldr_load_by_name's store pointer, moved on every 256 bytes.
The byte ldr_get_2bits builds, two bits at a time from the serial data line, before ldr_get_byte inverts it.
Read only by BIT $80 in ldr_get_block, to spend three cycles; its value does not matter.
The KERNAL's flag for the Shift and Commodore keys switching the font; loader_boot sets it to $80, which locks them out.
The KERNAL's flag for the video standard, 1 on a PAL machine and 0 on an NTSC one; loader_boot reads it to choose the block receiver's timing.

The boot file's first 12 bytes are a BASIC line, 10 SYS2061, so that the file also starts when it is loaded with LOAD"*",8 to $0801: SYS 2061 is $080D, where boot_copy_down then sits. Loaded with ,8,1 as the manual says, the file lands here and these bytes are never run.
Run only when the boot file was loaded to $0801 (SYS 2061): copies its 102 bytes from $0801 down to $02A7, where they were meant to go, and jumps to boot_load_loader.
The file name the boot asks the KERNAL for, "CO*": the first file whose name starts CO, which is COPYRIGHT 1985, the fast loader.

The boot: every BASIC vector at $0300-$030B points here, so the KERNAL's LOAD ends by jumping in as soon as this file is in. Turns the KERNAL's messages off, loads "CO*" from drive 8 to its own address ($C000) and jumps to loader_boot there.

29 bytes nothing runs: the tail of an instruction and two copy loops that shift $0C68-$0C7B down by one and $0C7C-$0CC4 down by two, an earlier form of the PAL patch that loader_boot makes at $C03F to the block receiver at $0C35 (one byte off from it). Left in the boot file from another build.

The BASIC vectors IERROR, IMAIN, ICRNCH, IQPLOP, IGONE and IEVAL, every one set to $02C4 (boot_load_loader). The boot file loads over them, so whatever BASIC does next after the LOAD lands in the boot.
The KERNAL's IRQ, BRK and NMI vectors in RAM; loader_boot keeps the first six bytes in ldr_vectors and ldr_reset_machine puts them back.
The KERNAL's NMI vector, low byte; loader_boot points it at ldr_nmi ($0906).
The KERNAL's NMI vector, high byte; loader_boot sets it to $09.
The KERNAL's STOP vector, low byte; loader_boot points it at ldr_stop_never ($0B15).
The KERNAL's STOP vector, high byte; loader_boot sets it to $0B.

The page of variables every part shares, cleared by loader_boot before the first load: $081F is the event chosen, $083D says whether the menu must be loaded again, $085D-$085E is where the menu resumes, $085F flags a load under way, $087D is the number of joysticks, $087E the letter of the file being loaded and $089F the number of the file in memory.
Where boot_copy_down reads the boot file from when it was loaded to BASIC's start: $0801-$0866, 102 bytes.
$FF when something has been loaded over the menu since it last ran, set by ldr_load_done and by loader_boot; the menu's entry clears it, and ldr_restart reloads the menu only while it is set.
The high byte of the address the menu jumps to when it is started again ($085D is the low byte); 0 means start at the top. ldr_nmi clears it, so RUN/STOP and RESTORE always land on the main menu.
$36 while a file is loading, 0 once it is in: ldr_run_file loads again when a load was cut short.
The number of joysticks, 1 or 2; loader_boot sets 2, and the menu shows it as the digit in option 5.
The one-letter name of the file being loaded, from its record, which ldr_load_by_name sends to the drive code.
The number of the file loaded last, so ldr_run_file can skip a load when the file is still there.

The loader's three entries, which every part calls by these fixed addresses. $0900 jumps to ldr_restart (reload the menu); loader_boot points it at $C0DC for the first two loads, then back. $0903 jumps to ldr_run_file (load file X and start it).
The low byte of the JMP at $0900 (ldr_jump_table), changed by loader_boot with $0902.
The high byte of the JMP at $0900, which loader_boot points at $C0DC for the boot's two loads and back at $0AD0 after them ($0901 is the low byte).

The NMI handler (RESTORE), set at $0318 and $FFFA by loader_boot. With RUN/STOP held as well (row 7 of the keyboard read through CIA 1) it clears $085E, so the menu starts from its top, and goes to ldr_restart: back to the menu from anywhere. Without RUN/STOP it puts CIA 1's port directions back and returns. Its first byte is a SEI, which ldr_load_file changes to RTI ($40) while a file loads and back after, so RESTORE does nothing during a load.

Writes the 256 bytes at $0E00 (the world records) back to track 18 sector 13 of side 1, asking for side 1 first if another side is in (ldr_check_side, ldr_insert_side). Command 4 to the drive code, then the 256 bytes. The menu calls it at $18AE.

Blanks the screen (ldr_blank) and asks the drive code (command 3, track 18, sector 0) for one byte of the disk's header sector, the side number: byte $97 there, the eighth character of the disk name, is $01 on side 1 and $02 on side 2, the only byte of the sector that reads 1 on one side and 2 on the other. Keeps a value below 5, makes a "G" 4 and anything else 0, and stores it in $16, which ldr_load_file ANDs with the side a file record wants.

Asks for the other disk side: colours the whole screen cyan in colour RAM, writes "INSERT WINTER GAMES    SIDE n" on line 6 and "THEN PRESS JOYSTICK BUTTON" on line 8 of the screen at $0400, both in white, with the side digit from str_side_digits by Y (the side a file record wants), turns the screen on in the ROM font (ldr_text_screen) and waits for fire on either joystick.
The RTS that ends ldr_insert_side; str_side_digits is read from one byte before it, so Y = 0 would read this byte.
The side digit for ldr_insert_side, read at $09C7+Y and $09CB+Y for Y = 1, 2 or 4: spaces, then "1", "2" and "1". Then the two lines of the prompt in ASCII, 29 bytes each from $09D0 and $09ED.
The side digits proper, read at $09CB+Y: "1" for side 1 at $09CC, "2" for side 2 at $09CD, and "1" again at $09CF for the 4 that a "G" disk gives.

"INSERT WINTER GAMES    SIDE 1", 29 characters in ASCII order, which the game's own fonts and the ROM's lower-case font both show as capitals. ldr_insert_side writes it to line 6 and puts the wanted side's digit over the last character.
"THEN PRESS JOYSTICK BUTTON" and three spaces, the prompt's second line, 29 characters in ASCII order.
The loader's second page, $0A00, which loader_boot's copy loop writes from $C24A; mid-way through str_press_button.

Loads the file whose record ldr_file_offset left at $15: checks the side in the drive against the record's side (offset 9) and asks for the right one until they match, keeps the file's number in $089F, makes ldr_nmi return at once (RTI) and starts CIA 2's timer A to raise one NMI it never acknowledges, which keeps RESTORE from raising another during the load. Then loads the file by its one-letter name (ldr_load_by_name) and ends through ldr_load_done. The branch at $0A47 goes to $0A49 whichever way it is taken, so ldr_unpack is never reached.

Run by nothing: the BEQ at $0A47 that would reach it was given an offset of 0. An unpacker for a run-length packed file: reads from the record's load address (offset 1) and writes to its destination (offset 3) until the record's end (offset 5); $BF n writes n zeros, $CF n v writes n copies of v, anything else is copied. Every record in this table has the same load address and destination but one ("?", $8100 to $1000), so it is the remains of another layout.

The end of every load: clears the load-in-progress flag $085F, sets $083D to $FF (the menu must be reloaded when it is next wanted), banks the KERNAL back in ($01 = $36), puts back the SEI at ldr_nmi and reads CIA 2's interrupt register, which acknowledges the held NMI so that RESTORE works again.
Stores A at the unpacker's destination pointer ($10) and moves it on. Used only by ldr_unpack.
Reads the next byte at the unpacker's source pointer ($12) and moves it on. Used only by ldr_unpack.
Back to the menu: resets the stack, puts the machine into a known state (ldr_reset_machine) and starts file 0, the menu, loading it first when $083D says the memory holds something else.

Loads file number X (0 the menu, 1 the opening ceremony, 3 the title, 4 to 10 the seven events) unless it is already in memory, then starts it: copies the record's entry address into the JMP at $0B07, waits for the raster to pass the bottom of the screen, banks the KERNAL in and jumps. A load is skipped when it is the file loaded last ($089F) and no load was cut short ($085F).
The loader's third page, $0B00, written by loader_boot's copy loop from $C34A; it starts inside ldr_run_file.
The low byte of the JMP at $0B07, which ldr_run_file sets to the file's entry point from its record.
The high byte of the JMP at $0B07, the file's entry point.
Turns file number X into the offset of its record in ldr_files, X times 12, kept in $15 and returned in X; keeps the number in $14. Returns A = $FF.
The STOP vector at $0328 points here: LDA #$FF and return, which tells the KERNAL that RUN/STOP is never pressed.

Puts the machine in the state every part starts from: waits for raster line $FB, restores the KERNAL's IRQ, BRK and NMI vectors at $0314 from ldr_vectors, sets the processor port ($00 = $2F, $01 = $36), zeroes the sprite and scroll registers of the video chip, sets the background colours from ldr_colours, silences the SID's voices (ldr_sid_voice) and filter, turns off CIA 2's interrupts and enables CIA 1's timer A interrupt, sets CIA 1's port A to output with every key column high, and selects video bank 0 ($DD00 bits 0-1).
The seven register values ldr_reset_machine writes to each SID voice: frequency and pulse width 0, control $08 (the test bit, which holds the oscillator silent), attack, decay, sustain and release 0.
The three background colours ldr_reset_machine writes to $D021-$D023: cyan, red and white.
The KERNAL's IRQ, BRK and NMI vectors ($0314-$0319) as loader_boot found them, kept so ldr_reset_machine can put them back; the NMI one is ldr_nmi by then.
Receives one byte from the drive code, two bits at a time (ldr_get_2bits four times), and returns it in A inverted, since the serial lines read low for a 1.
Receives two bits on the serial bus: waits for the clock line (bit 6 of $DD00) to go one way, takes the data line (bit 7) into $24, waits for it to go back and takes the next bit.
Blanks the screen ($D011 = $0B), turns the sprites off and waits for the raster to wrap past line 255 into a new frame.
Shows the text screen at $0400 in the ROM's upper- and lower-case font ($D018 = $17) and turns the display on ($D011 = $1B).
Sends the byte in A to the drive code, two bits at a time on the serial clock and data lines, after waiting for the drive to say it is ready.
The loader's fourth page, $0C00, written by loader_boot's copy loop from $C44A; it starts inside ldr_send_byte.

Sends the drive code a four-byte command: the command number in A, the byte in $1B, then X and Y (a track and a sector, or for command 2 the file's name in X). Commands seen: 2 load a file by name, 3 read the side byte, 4 write a sector, 5 read a sector.

Run by nothing in this game: receives 240-byte blocks from the drive, three bytes a round through the stack, EORs each with $F9 and stores it at ($17), for $1B blocks. loader_boot still shortens its delays for a PAL machine by moving $0C67-$0C7A and $0C7B-$0CC3 down (so the bytes here are the PAL form), and boot_leftover has another version of that patch: the routine was used by an earlier build of the loader.
Where loader_boot's PAL patch moves $0C67-$0C7A to, one byte down, in ldr_get_block.
The start of the 20 bytes loader_boot moves down by one on a PAL machine.
Where loader_boot's PAL patch moves $0C7B-$0CC3 to, two bytes down, in ldr_get_block.
The start of the 73 bytes loader_boot moves down by two on a PAL machine.
An operand loader_boot increases twice on a PAL machine (INC $0C97), in ldr_get_block's code: one of the timing changes for the PAL clock.
Two bytes before the file table, $4D and $60.

The loader's file table, twelve bytes a file: the name's one letter, then the load address, the destination, the end, the entry point (each low byte first, from offset 1) and the disk side (offset 9). 0 M the menu ($0F00, side 1), 1 O the opening ceremony (entry $8200), 2 "?" (never loaded), 3 T the title, 4 H Hot Dog, 5 I Biathlon, 6 S Speed Skating (at $4C00, entry $9400), 7 F Figure Skating, 8 J Ski Jump, 9 F Free Skating (the same file, entry $1005), 10 B Bobsled; 7 to 10 on side 2.
Offset 1 of every file record, read as $0CC4,X: the load address, low byte.
Offset 2 of every file record: the load address, high byte.
Offset 3 of every file record: the destination, low byte.
Offset 4 of every file record: the destination, high byte.
Offset 5 of every file record: the end, low byte.
Offset 6 of every file record: the end, high byte.
Offset 7 of every file record: the entry point, low byte.
Offset 8 of every file record: the entry point, high byte.
Offset 9 of every file record: the disk side (1 or 2), then two zeros (offsets 10 and 11) that nothing reads; the next record's letter follows. The table runs on to $0D46.
The loader's fifth page, $0D00, written by loader_boot's copy loop from $C54A; it falls inside file record 4 (Hot Dog, from $0CF3).
The middle of file record 10 (Bobsled, from $0D3B), past ldr_page_0d's reach.

Nine more twelve-byte records after the eleven the game uses (letters D, E, F, F, H and K among them, at addresses such as $8200, $8300 and $8000, sides 0), and the start of the code after them: nothing reads past record 10, since no file number above 10 is ever asked for. Left from another game's table.

Loads one file: command 2 with the file's letter in X, then reads the load address and the file's bytes from the drive code into memory from there. $AC is an escape: $AC $AC is one $AC, $AC $FF or $AC $F7 ends the file, and $AC with anything else is dropped.
Eight bytes nothing runs: another ending of the load loop, which jumps back to $0DC9.
The last byte of the loader file ($C636), copied here with the rest.

Track 18 sector 13 of side 1, read here by loader_boot and written back by ldr_save_records: the world records. On this disk every byte is 0 but one in each 20 ($0E11, $0E25 and so on), so the World Records screen shows empty bars.

The fast loader's start, run once at power-on. Silences the SID (loader_sid), copies the loader to $0900-$0DFF and clears $0800-$08FF for the variables every part shares, shortens the unused block receiver's delays on a PAL machine ($02A6 = 1), starts the drive code (loader_start_drive), sets $083D (the menu must be loaded) and two joysticks ($087D), points the NMI vector at ldr_nmi and the STOP vector at ldr_stop_never, keeps the IRQ vectors, parks the sprites, stops Shift and Commodore from switching the font, reads the world records into $0E00, then loads and runs the title (file 3) with $0900 pointed at $C0DC, so that the title's exit loads and runs the opening ceremony (file 1).

The 25 values loader_boot writes to SID registers $D400-$D418: each voice at frequency $0F0F, pulse width $0F0F, noise with the gate on ($81), attack and decay $0F, sustain and release $0F; filter 0 and volume 0, so nothing is heard.

Opens the drive's buffer channel ("#", channel 2) and its command channel with "B-E 2 0 18 5", which makes the drive run the code in track 18 sector 5 from buffer 0, then waits for the drive code to answer on the serial bus.
Opens the drive's command channel 15 with "B-E 2 0 18 5" (12 characters at str_block_execute), which starts the drive code.
OPEN 2,8,2,"#": a channel to a buffer in the drive, for the B-E command to load the code into.
"B-E 2 0 18 5", the DOS command that loads track 18 sector 5 into the drive's buffer on channel 2 and runs it; then "#", the buffer channel's name.

The loader as the file holds it, which loader_boot copies to $0900-$0DFF: the same bytes as $0900-$0DEC, but for those the game changes after the copy ($0B08, $0B96 and the PAL patch at $0C66-$0CC1). It stays here unused after the copy, since nothing loads over $C000.
The loader's source for $0A00-$0AFF (loader_copy_src's second page).
The rest of the source for $0A00-$0AFF, $0A40-$0AFF.
The loader's source for $0B00-$0BFF.
The rest of the source for $0B00-$0BFF, $0B40-$0BFF.
The loader's source for $0C00-$0CFF, the PAL-patched part of it before the patch.
The rest of the source for $0C00-$0CFF, $0C40-$0CFF.
The second part of the loader's source copy (loader_copy_src), $0D00-$0DEC at their own addresses; the file ends at $C636.

The processor's own vectors in the RAM under the KERNAL, used whenever a part banks the KERNAL out: NMI, set to ldr_nmi by loader_boot; reset, never set ($0000); IRQ, which each part sets to its own handler ($AC11 here, left by the opening ceremony).
